entities.summary: Frothar of Toul was a significant figure in medieval European history, serving as the bishop of Toul from 813 to 847. Born in 800 CE, he rose to prominence as the abbot of St. Evre's Abbey, Toul, before being appointed to the bishopric. As bishop, Frothar played a crucial role in the preservation and dissemination of Christian knowledge, collecting and preserving a vast collection of letters that have survived to this day. His legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing the development of medieval scholarship and the preservation of Christian texts. In his final years, Frothar worked to consolidate the power of the Church in the region, solidifying his own position as a key figure in the ecclesiastical hierarchy of 9th-century France. Frothar's surviving letters have provided valuable insights into the politics, culture, and spirituality of medieval Europe, offering a unique window into the lives of those who shaped the continent's history during this period. Through his efforts, Frothar of Toul has left an enduring impact on the world of scholarship and the Christian tradition.
